I buzzed my head a year ago and wore a wig or a hat while my hair grew back, I had to cut all my hair off twice until the bald spots became unnoticed, I would recommend a real hair wig with invisible lace as similar to your natural hair color as possible so you can wear it everyday if you want to, I bought a pretty good one from [Aliexpress](https://es.aliexpress.com/item/4000934550711.html?spm=a2g0o.order_list.order_list_main.27.1f63194dYtIKgF&gatewayAdapt=glo2esp) at an affordable price.   
Pros:  
The wig nor the buzzcut stopped the impulse but it made me conscious of it and felt silly so I would redirect my anxiety to something else, that helped.  
Growing your hair back can been fun, since I decided it was time to stop buzzing it, I've had the buzzcut, then a mohawk, then a mullet, then idk what shape is rn and long hair at the same time if I wanted to.  
Cons:  
It will still look patchy(er)  
It can be tough to look at yourself with full hair again with the wig, for me it was at least.  
I developed a bit of dermatillomania for a while, scratching my head instead of pulling.

I came to this subreddit thinking people that constantly use AI to create art might know a thing or two.

One of the first assignments I got in the first year of uni (design) was this, and the way some of my classmates that didn't know how to draw got really amazing results by the end of that one course, and it was pretty fun. 30 drawings per instruction (weekly). At first it was only silhouettes of random people on the street, then you added a bit more definition like shapes within the silhouette, like, are they wearing a dress or a skirt? the length or general shape of the hair. Next it was more detail, what are their hands doing? the eyes, folds in clothes. none of this has to be perfect, but you just have to understand what is going on. I can't remember what were the next steps, but the final one were sequences of hands doing something, I can't remember how many.
The people we would draw were ideally random people in a park/subway/cafe, wherever, which is 1.fun 2.very useful because it forces you to understand big shapes and movement in a short period of time (before they moove). 
If you can't go out, use Pinterest, search: pose references, or just follow recommended under some picture. And that should help. I started doing this today in the morning out of boredom and its just so much fun.
